xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2993: Strike landing wedges permanently when the strike agent is dead: transport failures demand a fresh head, recovery mail goes to a queue nobody reads, and strike-ready no-ops in 'recovering'

plan.title: Strike landing wedges permanently when the strike agent is dead: transport failures demand a fresh head, recovery mail goes to a queue nobody reads, and strike-ready no-ops in 'recovering'
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: Strike landings wedge permanently when the strike agent is dead. (1) Transport-level failures of the internal merge POST (fetch failed / ECONNREFUSED during a dashboard restart) are routed to agent recovery, which demands a fresh pushed HEAD for what is really an infra blip needing a plain retry. (2) When the strike session is unresumable, recovery feedback is queued to a mail directory nothing reads, yet the landing state becomes 'recovering' — terminal in practice because the patrol skips 'recovering' markers. (3) pan strike-ready cannot re-arm from 'recovering' at the same head, so the operator has no sanctioned retry short of inventing a new commit.
narratives.Proposal: Three coordinated fixes per the PRD (.pan/drafts/PAN-2993.md): (a) classify transport failures at the source (transport:true on StrikeMergeResult) and retry them at the same head via patrol re-claim with data-driven exponential backoff (strikeNextAttemptAt, 60s base, x2, 30min cap, 10-retry cap then needs_you); (b) widen messageAgent to return a MessageDeliveryOutcome so handleFailure can route undelivered recovery (mail-only queuing to a dead agent) straight to needs_you instead of 'recovering'; (c) let pan strike-ready re-arm from 'recovering' at the same head, clearing recovery and transport counters. New status fields are mirrored through the permanent-record sync so backoff state survives DB rebuilds.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Re-enabling session rotation on resume failure (PAN-1980 stays: no fresh-launch fallback)
- Changing the 3-cycle agent-recovery budget or the recovery message contents for genuinely agent-actionable failures
- Adding retry/backoff to any non-strike merge path (verified merge door, swarm merges)
- Draining or replaying the agent mail queue for dead agents
- Allowing same-head re-arm from 'landing' or 'landed' states
- Changing the StrikeLandingState union (no new states)
- Editing messageAgent callers outside strike landing

autoDecisions.summary: Transport failures detected at the source via transport:true on requestStrikeMerge's catch, not by regexing error strings downstream.
autoDecisions.rationale: Any throw inside the try means the endpoint never returned a verdict — that IS the transport class; string matching is fragile and the issue's observed 'fetch failed' is just one spelling.

autoDecisions.summary: Transport failures form a third class that silently retries at the same head, instead of being folded into NON_ACTIONABLE (which routes to needs_you).
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue's own analysis says these need 'a plain retry, not a new commit'; needs_you would still page the operator for every dashboard restart. The regex is extended anyway as a safety net for the supervised-crash path.

autoDecisions.summary: Backoff constants: 60s base, x2 per consecutive failure, 30min cap, 10 consecutive failures then needs_you; implemented as a strikeNextAttemptAt timestamp checked by the patrol, never setTimeout.
autoDecisions.rationale: Patrol-cycle-driven retry reuses the existing claim/lease machinery and keeps the module timer-free (fake-timers rule not triggered); the cap ensures a permanently dead endpoint still surfaces to the operator.

autoDecisions.summary: messageAgent's return type widens from Promise<void> to Promise<MessageDeliveryOutcome> rather than throwing on mail-only queuing.
autoDecisions.rationale: Throwing would change observable behavior for ~20 existing callers; a returned outcome is source-compatible (callers ignore the value) and fixes the false-success report at the root for future callers too.

autoDecisions.summary: Codex mid-turn .pending mail counts as delivered:true.
autoDecisions.rationale: The notify hook replays pending mail to a live session at turn end — guaranteed to be read; only mail queued for stopped/gated agents is undelivered.

autoDecisions.summary: Same-head re-arm added only for 'recovering' (alongside existing 'needs_you'); 'landing' still returns unchanged.
autoDecisions.rationale: Operator readiness is the recovery signal for a wedged landing, but re-arming a merge already in flight could double-land.

narrative.Action: Per PRD W1: add `transport?: boolean` to StrikeMergeResult and set `transport: true` in requestStrikeMerge's catch branch (src/lib/cloister/deacon-strike-landing.ts:48-50). Add `strikeTransportRetryCount?: number` and `strikeNextAttemptAt?: string` to StrikeLandingStatus (src/lib/strike-landing.ts). Mirror both new fields alongside the existing five strike fields in src/lib/pan-dir/records.ts:136-140 and src/lib/overdeck/review-status-record-sync.ts:114-118. Extend tests/unit/lib/cloister/deacon-strike-transport.test.ts with a rejected-fetch case asserting transport:true and a structured-HTTP-error case asserting transport is absent.

items.title: Given fetchImpl rejects, requestStrikeMerge returns { success: false, transport: true } with the error message preserved
Given the endpoint returns a structured HTTP error result, requestStrikeMerge returns success:false without the transport flag
The record builders in records.ts and review-status-record-sync.ts emit strikeTransportRetryCount and strikeNextAttemptAt so a status containing them round-trips with values preserved
Retry transport failures at the same head with patrol-driven exponential backoff and a needs_you cap

expected_outputs: deacon-strike-landing.test.ts passes including new transport-retry, backoff-skip, cap-escalation, and landed-clears-fields tests

narrative.Action: Per PRD W2: in src/lib/cloister/deacon-strike-landing.ts add constants TRANSPORT_BACKOFF_BASE_MS=60_000, TRANSPORT_BACKOFF_CAP_MS=1_800_000, MAX_TRANSPORT_RETRIES=10. Add handleTransportFailure(issueId, head, detail, status, deps): append attempt with outcome 'transport-failed'; count = (status.strikeTransportRetryCount ?? 0) + 1; if count >= MAX_TRANSPORT_RETRIES route to the existing needs_you block (feedback file + needsYou + state needs_you); else setStatus back to 'ready' at the same head with strikeTransportRetryCount=count and strikeNextAttemptAt = new Date(Date.parse(deps.now()) + min(cap, base * 2^(count-1))).toISOString(). In executeStrikeLanding's failure branch, route result.transport to handleTransportFailure, everything else to handleFailure. In patrolStrikeLandings' filter, skip candidates whose strikeNextAttemptAt > deps.now() (ISO string comparison). On the 'landed' transition also clear strikeTransportRetryCount and strikeNextAttemptAt (set undefined). Extend NON_ACTIONABLE with |fetch failed|ECONNREFUSED|ECONNRESET|socket hang up|ETIMEDOUT|EAI_AGAIN. Never use setTimeout — backoff is data compared against injected deps.now(). Add tests using the existing injected-deps pattern in tests/lib/cloister/deacon-strike-landing.test.ts.

Given strikeNextAttemptAt is later than deps.now(), patrolStrikeLandings skips the marker without claiming; once deps.now() passes the due time it claims and invokes mergeIssue again at the same head
Given strikeTransportRetryCount already at 9, a further transport failure sets state 'needs_you', writes the feedback file, and surfaces needsYou with the full attempt history
Given a merge resolves mergeStatus 'merged' after transport retries, the 'landed' transition clears strikeTransportRetryCount and strikeNextAttemptAt

Given a non-transport failure whose detail contains 'fetch failed' or 'ECONNREFUSED' (supervised-crash path), handleFailure routes it to needs_you and never sends the agent a fresh-HEAD recovery demand

narrative.Action: Per PRD W3: in src/lib/agents/messaging.ts export interface MessageDeliveryOutcome { delivered: boolean; queuedToMail: boolean; reason?: string } and change messageAgent's return type to Promise<MessageDeliveryOutcome>. Label every return path exactly per the PRD W3 table: paused/gated/stopped-gated mail paths -> delivered:false, queuedToMail:true with the gate reason; PAN-1980 no-rotation stop -> delivered:false, queuedToMail:true, reason:stopMsg; suspended/stopped successful resume -> delivered:true; fallback fresh-launch -> delivered from its computed flag; remote agent -> delivered:true; codex mid-turn .pending mail -> delivered:true with reason 'queued for turn-end delivery'; codex idle direct and final tmux delivery -> delivered from deliverAgentMessage(...).ok. The four existing throw sites stay throws. Do not edit any caller outside strike landing. Extend tests/unit/lib/agents/message-agent.test.ts to assert the returned outcome on the PAN-1980 path, a gated path, and a live-delivery path.

narrative.Action: Per PRD W6: update the strike handoff paragraphs in docs/SPECIALIST_WORKFLOW.md (currently lines 311-313) so they state: (1) transport-level merge-request failures (dashboard restart, connection refused) are retried by the Deacon at the same pushed HEAD with exponential backoff and never generate a rebase-and-repush recovery request; (2) a recovery message that cannot be delivered to a live strike session surfaces as needs-you immediately instead of leaving the landing in 'recovering'; (3) pan strike-ready <id> re-arms a 'recovering' landing at the same HEAD — the sanctioned operator retry.
